subject: Operations
title: The Case for Global Operations
description: A quick, practical guide to The Case for Global Operations.

hook.text: An iPhone: designed in California, chips from Taiwan, assembled in China, sold in 175 countries. That's global ops.

buildup.text: Companies go global to access cheaper labor, larger markets, specialized skills, and natural resources.

discovery.text: Global operations let firms produce where costs are lowest and sell where demand is highest—arbitraging the world.

twist.text: Going global adds complexity: time zones, languages, regulations, and logistics that domestic operations never face.

climax.text: The most successful global firms balance cost advantage with the complexity cost of managing across borders.

punchline.text: Global ops offer huge gains—and huge complexity.

quiz.question: Why do companies globalize operations?
options: To access cheaper labor and larger markets
